summary: Chile's foreign ministry publishes a table giving, for each nationality, whether a visa (autorización previa o visa) is required and the stay. It marks US, Canadian and UK nationals, for example, as needing no visa, with 90 days; Chile's transitory stay permit (permanencia transitoria) allows a stay of up to 90 days, and the table gives shorter stays for some nationalities, such as 30 days for Singapore. Those who need a visa apply for it through Chile's online consular services.

visaTypes.name: Prior authorisation or visa (Autorización previa o visa)

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile — Autorización previa o visa

stayDays.text: La autorización previa o visa puede autorizar una o múltiples entradas y permite una estadía de hasta 90 días.

extendable.text: Una vez en Chile, el permiso de permanencia puede ser prorrogado por 90 días, a través del Servicio Nacional de Migraciones del Ministerio del Interior.

name.text: La autorización previa o visa puede autorizar una o múltiples entradas y permite una estadía de hasta 90 días.

method.text: La autorización previa o visa es otorgada por los consulados chilenos en el exterior y exigida, por motivos calificados de interés nacional o por motivos de reciprocidad internacional, a los nacionales de ciertos países para ingresar a Chile como titulares de permanencia transitoria.

visaTypes.name: Extension of transitory stay (Prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria)

fee.notes: Fee (pago de derechos) of USD 100. Children and adolescents are exempt.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Migraciones — Prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria

stayDays.text: Si eres titular de un permiso de Permanencia Transitoria, cualquiera haya sido su duración original, podrás prorrogarla por una sola vez, por hasta noventa días corridos.

extendable.text: Si eres titular de un permiso de Permanencia Transitoria, cualquiera haya sido su duración original, podrás prorrogarla por una sola vez, por hasta noventa días corridos.

method.text: La solicitud de prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria se realiza en el Portal de Trámites Digitales del Servicio Nacional de Migraciones (SERMIG), ingresando con ClaveÚnica o con la cuenta creada por la persona postulante para esos fines.

passportValidity.text: Chile's migration service says the transitory stay permit cannot run past the validity of your passport or travel document, and the UK Foreign Office says your passport should have an expiry date after the day you plan to leave Chile. The migration service lists an identity card, without the need for a passport, as a document for entering Chile only for nationals of Mercosur countries and Bolivia.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Migraciones — Permanencia Transitoria

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Chile. Canada's travel advice says to make sure you get travel insurance that includes coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Chile

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement for visitors to mainland Chile. The UK Foreign Office says that to enter Rapa Nui (Easter Island) you must show a return ticket.

source.name: UK FCDO — Chile travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: Chile's foreign ministry says every foreigner entering as the holder of a transitory stay permit must show the border authority lawful means of support for their stay. No official source we could read states an amount. The ministry lists proof of the applicant's own economic means among the requirements for a prior authorisation or visa.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile — Información sobre visas para ingresar a Chile

declarations.name: Sworn agricultural declaration (Declaración Jurada SAG)
declarations.submitWindow: From one day before arrival online, or on arrival
declarations.text: SAG's Digital Affidavit for Entry to Chile asks you to declare the plant and animal origin products, goods and currencies (money) you carry in your luggage or means of transport. It says the procedure is free of charge, individual and mandatory for all persons over 18 years of age, and that the form can be completed with or without an internet connection, up to one day before your entry, and is valid only for the date of arrival you indicate. SAG's information page says the declaration is made on special forms (digital or paper) and that failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

source.name: Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero (SAG) — Digital Affidavit for Entry to Chile (Declaración Jurada), start step

alsoStatedOn.name: Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero (SAG) — Declaración Jurada SAG de ingreso a Chile (information page)

declarations.name: Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM)
declarations.text: Chile's migration service says the PDI hands you the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) when you enter Chile, and lists a valid TUM as a document that allows you to leave the country.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Migraciones — Guía de ayuda N°5: documentos de viaje para ingresar o salir de Chile

currencyLimits.text: Chile's customs service says that if you enter or leave Chile with cash or bearer negotiable instruments of USD 10,000 or more, or the equivalent in other currencies including the Chilean peso, you must declare it to customs.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Aduanas de Chile — Declaración de Dinero

notes: The Agricultural and Livestock Service (SAG) says Chilean law requires people to declare under oath, on special forms (digital or paper), any plants, animals, products of plant or animal origin (including handicrafts), agricultural chemical or biological products, veterinary medicines or animal feed they bring in. It says SAG border inspectors check them whatever their quantity, packaging or how long ago they were obtained; products that do not meet the requirements are not allowed in and are destroyed, and failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

overstay.text: Holders of a Permanencia Transitoria permit who stay up to 180 calendar days after it expires are fined from half to 10 UTM, with an exception for certain residents. Those who stay more than 180 calendar days after expiry are fined 1 to 10 UTM. Fines are cut by 50% when offenders report themselves to the Migration Service or the Police and this leads to the infringement being detected. Children and adolescents are exempt from all fines. To leave Chile, all fines for migration infringements must be paid, through the SERMIG Portal de Trámites and the web platform of the Tesorería General de la República.

source.name: Ministerio del Interior (Chile) — Ley 21.325 de Migración y Extranjería (BCN text)
source.instrument: Ley 21.325, arts. 107 (expired ≤180 days), 119 (expired >180 days), 121 (50% reduction on self-report)

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing, mugging and thefts from vehicles are very common throughout Chile, including inside airports, churches, hotels and bus stations. The Government of Canada advises a high degree of caution in Chile due to ongoing demonstrations, civil unrest and crime, and says armed assaults and robberies have increased in recent years. Canada says Chile is located in a very active seismic zone where earthquakes and tsunamis can occur anywhere, and the UK says major earthquakes are a risk.

The UK Foreign Office says you must show a reservation registered with SERNATUR or an invitation letter from the provincial delegation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport: Chile's foreign ministry publishes a table giving, for each nationality, whether a visa is required and the stay. For example, it marks US, Canadian, UK, Mexican, Australian, Japanese and Israeli nationals as needing no visa, with 90 days; Singapore, Malaysian and Macao passport holders as needing no visa, with 30 days; for Belizean and Indonesian passports it gives two figures (30 or 90 days, and 60 or 90 days). Nationalities that need a prior authorisation or visa apply for it through Chile's online consular services.

faq.question: Is there still a reciprocity fee to enter Chile?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states a reciprocity or arrival fee for visa-exempt visitors.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Chile?
faq.answer: Chile's migration service says the transitory stay permit allows a stay of up to 90 days; the foreign ministry's table gives 30 days for Singapore, Malaysian and Macao passports, and two figures for Belizean and Indonesian passports (30 or 90 days, and 60 or 90 days). The migration service says the permit can be extended once, by up to 90 calendar days, through the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones' digital portal, for a fee of USD 100 (children and adolescents are exempt), and that you must start the extension before the original period on your Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) ends.

faq.question: Are there extra rules for visiting Easter Island?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says stays on Rapa Nui are limited to 30 consecutive days for all travellers and that you must show a round-trip ticket and proof of a reservation of accommodation authorised by local authorities, and complete the Rapa Nui Entry Form; the UK Foreign Office tells people travelling on a full British citizen passport that they must show a reservation registered with SERNATUR, the national tourism service, or an invitation letter from the provincial delegation.

faq.question: What is the SAG declaration?
faq.answer: The Agricultural and Livestock Service (SAG) says Chilean law requires people to declare under oath, on special forms (digital or paper), any plants, animals, products of plant or animal origin (including handicrafts), agricultural chemical or biological products, veterinary medicines or animal feed they bring in. It says the digital declaration is free; SAG inspectors check what is declared whatever its quantity, and failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

faq.question: Do Venezuelan or Haitian citizens need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: Yes. Chile's foreign ministry's table marks both nationalities as needing a visa. The ministry says the prior authorisation or visa (autorización previa o visa) is granted by Chilean consulates abroad and must be applied for on the online consular services platform.
